subject: Capacity runaway: priority customer experiencing throttling and 5xx errors
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Meyer <tmeyer@catalystpay.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throttling on our reserved pool

Jonas / Redwood team —

We're seeing a sudden ramp in 5xx errors and token queueing on our reserved capacity this morning. Starting ~07:45 PDT our production traffic to model redwood-14b-fast started returning 5xxs and end-to-end latency jumped from ~180ms to >1.5s. Throughput reported on your dashboard shows a 40% drop against our committed QPS and GPU utilization in the pool is pinned at >95%.

I've attached an excerpt of the API error log and a short sample trace. Impact: approximately 25% of requests failing, downstream user-facing errors for our invoicing flow. This is a priority outage for us (CatalystPay) and we're mobilizing SRE + Ops. Please advise immediate mitigations (fallback models, capacity burst, crediting) and ETA to restore committed throughput.

Thanks —
Elena Park
Head of Engineering, CatalystPay
Elena.park@catalystpay.com
Attachment: catalystpay_error_log_excerpt.txt
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throttling on our reserved pool

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 8:12 AM Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com> wrote:
> Jonas / Redwood team —
> ...

Elena — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs. We're treating this as P1. Initial triage: tagging Ops and Engineering now, and we'll stand up a short bridge.

Immediate asks for us to act fast:
- Can you confirm whether any bulk/cron jobs started around 07:30-08:00 PDT? (We see a burst pattern consistent with a scheduled job.)
- Is it acceptable for Redwood to flip CatalystPay traffic to a compatible hosted model variant for 30-120 minutes as a fallback while we stabilize the reserved pool?

We're attaching an internal snapshot of the capacity dashboard to this thread and will send a play-by-play. ETA for first mitigation attempt: 25-40 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: initial findings from pool metrics

Internal summary (not for customer until we confirm mitigations):
- Observed: sustained GPU utilization >95% across the dedicated pool serving CatalystPay; queue depth increasing and avg token generation latency trending to 1.2s+.
- Telemetry: KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% coincident with a spike in short-sequence requests at 07:38. Batching sizes increased due to a misapplied canary change in the customer's routing config (we're seeing 2x batching on some endpoints).
- Hypothesis: a scheduled background job (customer side) + a canary config change caused inefficient batching leading to queueing and downstream 5xxs when GPU resources were exhausted.

Proposed immediate actions (we can do all in concert):
1) Ask CatalystPay to pause non-essential background jobs (Jonas to request).
2) Enable 2-hour burst capacity on the pool to buy headroom (Aditya to authorize).
3) Roll back routing canary that modified batch sizing (Marissa to execute).
4) If rollback + burst don't restore SLA in 40m, fail traffic to hosted fallback (redwood-14b-stable) with traffic-shaping and graceful degrade.

Estimated time-to-stable if actions applied: 30-50 minutes. I'll join the bridge and run the rollback.

- Lauren
VP, Customer Ops
From: CatalystPay SRE <sre@catalystpay.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com>, Tom Meyer <tmeyer@catalystpay.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throttling on our reserved pool

Thanks for the rapid triage. Confirmed: we had a nightly reconciliation job misfired at 07:35 PDT that overlapped with higher-than-usual user traffic — that should not have happened. We're pausing that job now.

CatalystPay asks: if you enable burst headroom, will there be any billing delta or credits? Procurement (Tom Meyer) is on this thread and wants clarity on financial exposure for the burst and any service-level credits for the impact window. Also please keep us posted if a model fallback will change response characteristics.

- CatalystPay SRE (on behalf of Elena)
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com>, sre@catalystpay.com
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throttling on our reserved pool

CatalystPay — quick update and plan:
- We've authorized a 2-hour burst for your dedicated pool (effective immediately) and initiated a rollback of the routing canary that increased batch sizing.
- We've also opened an internal ops bridge (OPS-9823). Early telemetry shows queue depth beginning to reduce; 5xx rate down from ~25% to ~8% in the first 10 minutes.
- If you prefer we can fail overflow traffic to redwood-14b-stable for up to 90 minutes while we validate cache warm-up — we'll coordinate the exact endpoints and keep response semantics in mind.

Regarding procurement: Lauren, Marissa — please include a proposed credit for the incident window and an explicit summary of billing for the burst. Tom — our usual approach is not to charge unexpected bursts during incidents; we'll follow up with a formal credit proposal for May 21 impact.

Next update in 30 minutes or sooner with metrics.

Jonas
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@catalystpay.com>, sre@catalystpay.com
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident wrap: mitigation complete and next steps

Elena / CatalystPay — final update for the day:
- Mitigations applied: routing canary rollback, background job pause (customer), 2-hour burst enabled and circuit-limited overflow to redwood-14b-stable for low-latency endpoints.
- Current state: 5xxs reduced to <1%, avg latency restored to ~200ms, throughput at or above committed QPS. GPU utilization normalized to ~65%.
- Root cause: concurrent scheduled reconciliation job + canary-induced batching increased effective token-per-request and saturated the dedicated pool.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We're proposing a 10% credit for the customer billing for the incident window (May 21 07:35–10:00 PDT). Marissa will draft the credit memo and Tom (procurement) and Elena will be copied.
- Follow-up actions: Marissa/Aditya to run a post-incident runbook and a safe-guard that prevents canary changes from doubling batching without explicit approval by Redwood; Rishi will coordinate a short architecture review to recommend safe auto-burst thresholds.

If you want a 1:1 exec readout, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge with our CTO and your Head of Ops tomorrow.

Appreciate your patience — we'll send the postmortem with telemetry links to the Drive folder and the Jira ticket OPS-9823 by Monday EOD.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Ops
Attachment: capacity-dashboard-snapshot.png
